full_judgment: 7. The points raised by the learned counsel merit consideration. Leave is therefore granted to consider the following points: "(II)Because the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering that the trial court found actual exclusive possession of the land of suit jamas with the defendants which finding was not reversed by the appellate court, but the High Court Division erroneously by making a fresh appreciation only of oral evidences found possession of the plain-tiffs disregarding the vital evidences of D.Ws. 2-5 and presumption of possession available under finally published R. S. and S. A. khatians along' with up-to dated real receipts and series of registered deeds Exhibit D series since 1961 produced by the defendants, (III) Because the High Court Division committed error of law in not overriding the appellate court findings on the issue of title in the premises of provisions of sections 89 and 181 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and in the light of reported age old decisions of the superior courts as regards incidents of service tenancy distinguished from occupancy rights of other tenants."
